decisions: PIECE 3 - THE RATE FREEZE IS NOT GATED ON payout_id, unlike commission_sar beside it. That lock is about DRIVER commission being frozen into a payout snapshot; the customer rate is a different party's money and has nothing to do with whether the driver has been paid. Reusing the gate would tie two unrelated freezes together.

PIECE 3 - A TRIP WITH NO PROJECT STAMPS NOTHING and keeps its NULL, matching 0128's refusal to invent a rate for the single direct-customer trip. And the rate is NOT nulled when leaving delivered (unlike commission_sar): 0128's model is that a trip carrying a project carries that project's rate, so clearing it on a correction would erase what the backfill deliberately set. Re-delivering re-stamps, mirroring the station re-take rule.
PIECE 3 - FAILS CLOSED: if the project read errors, the whole stage move is refused rather than completing a delivery with an unstamped rate.

PIECE 3 - KNOWN COSMETIC CONSEQUENCE: a trip created from now on carries rate_sar NULL until delivered, while every pre-0128 trip was backfilled regardless of stage. ProjectsBoard renders rate_sar ?? 0, so a NEW scheduled trip reads 0 there until delivery. Self-correcting, and explicitly NOT a reason to stamp at creation - the snapshot records the price at the moment the trip became billable.

PIECE 4 - THE SCREEN EXISTS FOR BACK-DATING, not for everyday raises. The triggers already record a change entered today; only a dated row can say 'this salary applied from March'. The screen's other job is showing the timeline every payroll figure resolves through.

PIECE 4 - THE HONESTY BLOCK IS THE DESIGN. A back-dated row legitimately re-costs reported months, so the form states which month the recalculation starts from BEFORE the save, computed from the DATE ALONE rather than previewing a server number - the reader can check the rule instead of trusting a figure.

PIECE 4 - BASELINES ARE GUARDED TWICE: lock badge and NO delete control in the UI (not a disabled one - there is no case where removing it is right), and removeSalaryChange refuses them server-side. Deleting a baseline would make the earliest months resolve to nothing, which reads as a salary of zero rather than an error.

PIECE 4 - addSalaryChange DOES NOT WRITE drivers.salary_sar. That would fire the trigger and record a SECOND row dated today, turning one back-dated correction into two rows saying different things. The form owns the current value; the screen owns the timeline.

THE STAFF DETAIL NEVER SHOWED SALARY AT ALL - editable on the form, displayed nowhere, while the driver detail had shown it all along. Wiring the history button added the cell too, deliberately together: a salary with no timeline beside it is exactly the arrangement that let the value drift unnoticed until 0125.

INCIDENT - I COMMITTED THE BLANK auto-postool TEMPLATE OVER THIS FILE (commit 7b29c65). A python script errored BEFORE writing, and the `git add` chained after it with && still ran against whatever the auto-tool had left on disk. CLAUDE.md section 5 warns about exactly this. The real lesson is narrower than 'write and add in one command': the add must be conditional on the write having SUCCEEDED, and the staged blob must be inspected before committing - `git diff --cached --stat` showing a SHRINK is the tell.
